title: How to brief an AI companion toy project
description: A companion toy brief should explain the intended users and the experience you want to develop. A clear brief also gives the development team a basis for discussing product requirements and evaluation.
outline: Bring the brief to your development discussion

body.text: Define the intended users
Write down the age group, intended setting and role of a parent or supervising adult. Include the destination market and any requirements already agreed by your business.
Describe the interaction

Give a short example of what the user might say or do and the response you expect. Explain which interactions matter most. Ask the development team to confirm which requirements can be supported by the proposed product.
Specify content boundaries

List the topics and situations the product should handle carefully. Describe your expectations for inappropriate requests, missing information and adult involvement. These expectations belong in the requirements and evaluation plan.
Discuss memory and information

Explain what the product should remember, who should control that information and how users should be able to change or remove it. Ask for a clear description of the proposed information handling before agreeing the scope.
Include the physical product

Bring your design, branding, power and connectivity requirements into the brief. If you have a reference product, explain which parts of it matter to your project. Confirm specifications and sample arrangements with the supplier.
Agree the evaluation
Prepare representative interactions and define what an acceptable result looks like. Decide which product documents and demonstrations you need to review before proceeding.
Bring the brief to your development discussion
You can begin with a short document covering users, interaction, content, memory and product requirements. Mark unanswered questions so they can be discussed explicitly.

title: What to define before developing an AI office assistant
description: An office assistant project needs a clear description of the work it should support. Start with one task and the people responsible for its output.
outline: Prepare a brief your team can review

body.text: Describe the current task
Write down the steps your team follows today. Identify the input, tools and final output. Explain where people make decisions and what usually causes exceptions.
Identify the information
List the documents, records or systems relevant to the task. Note who owns the information, who may access it and how it changes. Use a sanitised example for an initial discussion.
Define the requested support

Describe what you want the assistant to produce or do at each step. Separate a suggestion for a person to review from an action performed in another system. Ask the development team to confirm the available capability.
Set approval and exception requirements

Decide which outputs need human review. Explain what should happen when information is incomplete, a tool is unavailable or a request falls outside the task. These requirements should be part of the proposed scope.
Discuss deployment and responsibilities
Share hosting, data-handling and access requirements. Ask who will operate the system, maintain the information and handle changes. Confirm the proposed dependencies and costs for the arrangement.
Agree the evaluation

Choose representative examples and the expected result for each one. Include exceptions as well as routine tasks. Define the evidence you need to decide whether the proposed assistant meets the requirement.
Prepare a brief your team can review
Bring the task, information, review points and evaluation examples into one document. A shared brief gives business and technical decision-makers a concrete basis for the development discussion.

title: Questions to ask an AI development partner
description: Before agreeing an AI product or workflow project, ask for a clear account of the proposed work and the evidence behind it. The answers should help your team decide what to evaluate and who will be responsible.
outline: What has the team actually delivered?
What is included in the proposed scope?
How will the work be evaluated?
How will information and access be handled?
What documents and commercial conditions apply?
Use the answers to prepare your decision

body.text: What has the team actually delivered?

Ask for examples relevant to the work you need. Clarify the team's contribution, the scope delivered and which materials the client has authorised for sharing. A workflow example and a hardware delivery example demonstrate different types of work.
What is included in the proposed scope?
Request a written description of features, integrations, documents and deliverables. List the assumptions and items that still need assessment. Agree how changes to the brief will be handled.
How will the work be evaluated?

Discuss demonstrations, sample arrangements and representative tasks. Define the result you expect and the evidence required to review it. For a product, confirm the model and specifications being evaluated.
Who handles development and production?

Clarify who performs software, hardware and manufacturing work. Ask which activities are completed by the team and which involve other parties. Confirm the responsibilities that apply to your project.
How will information and access be handled?
For an enterprise project, discuss the information involved, permissions, hosting and operating responsibilities. Ask for the proposed arrangement and the conditions affecting it.
What documents and commercial conditions apply?
Confirm the product-specific documentation, price basis, delivery arrangements and ongoing support. Record outstanding questions before agreeing a commitment.
Use the answers to prepare your decision
Bring the evidence, scope, evaluation and responsibilities into a short review document. Your team can then assess the proposed project against its actual requirement.
